comments.content: The self-clear mask is a hard-coded literal (`0x32`) that duplicates the CTRL bit decode performed later in the same file (`wdata[1]`/`wdata[4]`/`wdata[5]` in the write-action block). Current behavior is correct (and matches `Doc/Reg_v_0_0.md`: [1] SOFT_RST, [4] CLR_CNT, [5] CLR_FIFO), but any future change to the CTRL bit map must be edited in two unrelated places with no compile-time coupling, silently desynchronizing the mask from the decode. Consider deriving the mask from named bit positions shared with the decode.
comments.suggestion_code:
// CTRL 自清零位（与下方 wdata[1]/wdata[4]/wdata[5] 的译码共享同一组位位置）
    localparam CTRL_SOFT_RST_POS = 1;   // SOFT_RST
    localparam CTRL_CLR_CNT_POS  = 4;   // CLR_CNT
    localparam CTRL_CLR_FIFO_POS = 5;   // CLR_FIFO
    wire [31:0] ctrl_selfclear_mask = wstrb[0]
        ? ((32'h1 << CTRL_SOFT_RST_POS) | (32'h1 << CTRL_CLR_CNT_POS) | (32'h1 << CTRL_CLR_FIFO_POS))
        : 32'h0000_0000;

comments.content: `run.ps1` now forwards `+seed`/`+n_rand` whenever the parameter is bound (`$PSBoundParameters.ContainsKey`), and this recipe always binds both. A plain `make run` (SEED=0/NRAND=0 defaults) therefore passes `+seed=0 +n_rand=0`, which the testbenches treat as explicit values: the run silently drops to 0 random transactions (tb_dvp2ax_stream defaults to 400, tb_vrf_axil_demo to 250) and to a fixed seed, whereas `demo`/`dvp` still use the testcase defaults and `regress` suppresses the 0 case via `$(NRAND_ARG)` (header note: `0 = 沿用用例默认值`). `fault`'s hard-coded `-Nrand 0` now carries the same new meaning. If 0 is meant to mean "unspecified", forward with `$(NRAND_ARG)` here as well; otherwise document the per-target difference explicitly.
